howto.name: Meet the basic requirements
howto.text: Be at least 18 with a high school diploma or equivalent and a U.S. Social Security number.

howto.name: Complete the 63-hour pre-license course
howto.text: Finish Florida's state-approved 63-hour sales associate pre-license course and pass its end-of-course exam.

howto.name: Get fingerprinted
howto.text: Submit electronic fingerprints through a state-approved vendor for your background check.

howto.name: Apply to the DBPR
howto.text: Apply to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and receive your exam authorization.

howto.name: Pass the Florida state exam
howto.text: Pass the 100-question Florida sales associate exam (75% or higher) at a Pearson VUE testing center.

howto.name: Activate your license under a broker
howto.text: Join a licensed Florida broker, such as Adams, Cameron & Co., to activate your license and start working.

New Smyrna Beach is one of Volusia County's most desirable coastal towns, known for its beaches, Flagler Avenue, and a strong second-home and relocation market. Here's exactly how to get licensed, and what the local market looks like for a new agent.

How do you get a real estate license in New Smyrna Beach?

You earn the Florida real estate sales associate license, valid statewide. There is no separate New Smyrna Beach license. Be 18+ with a high school diploma, complete the 63-hour pre-license course, get fingerprinted, apply to the DBPR, pass the state exam (75% to pass), and activate under a broker. Most people finish in two to four months. Full detail is in our Florida licensing guide.

Is New Smyrna Beach a good market for a new real estate agent?

Yes, with a higher-end tilt. New Smyrna Beach draws second-home buyers, retirees, and relocating professionals, with desirable beachside and riverfront property alongside mainland neighborhoods. Higher price points can mean larger commissions per deal, but they also reward an agent who genuinely knows the market. Across Volusia County, about 900 homes sell each month at a $343,000 median, and coastal towns like New Smyrna often command a premium to that.

Why New Smyrna Beach earned the nickname “Florida’s Secret Pearl,” and what that means for your market

New Smyrna Beach was founded in 1768 by Dr. Andrew Turnbull and named after his wife’s birthplace in ancient Greece. The town carries that European heritage and the nickname “Florida’s Secret Pearl” reflects a market reality: buyers seeking New Smyrna are often choosing it deliberately, not settling. They’ve done research. They’re not chasing Miami or Tampa celebrity; they’re after a refined, walkable coastal town with genuine character and a strong water-sports culture. For an agent, that means you’re not competing on flash or lowest price. You’re telling the story of a specific, intentional place.

The surf culture creates a lifestyle segment with real market power

Surfer magazine has recognized New Smyrna Beach as one of America’s best surf towns, and that recognition is not marketing hype. The town has world-class breaks, a genuine community of surfers and water-sports enthusiasts, and a culture that blends beach practicality with artistic identity. This creates a distinct buyer pool that inland agents never encounter: young professionals buying their first beachside home, experienced surfers relocating for the waves, and families wanting their children raised in a water-sports community. Agents who understand this niche, who know the local breaks, the beach neighborhoods, and the water-sports calendar, have genuine credibility with these buyers and can command higher positioning than agents treating all coastal properties as generic beach real estate.

Flagler Avenue and the walkable waterfront district: a real skill for coastal agents

Flagler Avenue spans five lively blocks from the river to the ocean, lined with independent boutiques, surf shops, artisan markets, and established restaurants like the Breakers, operating since the early 1900s with beachfront dining and fresh seafood. This walkability premium, this sense of place, attracts a buyer with specific priorities: proximity to dining and local shopping, not strip malls; the rhythm of a real community, not sprawl. Agents who can speak authentically to Flagler Avenue’s history, the independent merchants, and which residential neighborhoods offer true walking distance to the district have developed a skill that purely transactional agents never build. It’s about understanding the lifestyle premium that drives waterfront and near-waterfront buyers to pay more for less square footage.

The Northeast relocation and second-home market shapes New Smyrna’s buyer profile

New Smyrna Beach has become a magnet for retirees relocating from the Northeast and for second-home buyers from across the country seeking a refined, less-crowded alternative to major tourist destinations. The median home price in New Smyrna sits around $490,000, significantly above Volusia County’s $343,000 median, reflecting this higher-end buyer composition. Neighborhoods like Venetian Bay, Isles of Sugar Mill, and the North Beach corridor move quickly, especially waterfront and newer construction. These are buyers with seasoned real-estate knowledge, experience in multiple markets, and often substantial resources. An agent working New Smyrna well understands the Northeast buyer’s comparison framework, helps them navigate the relocation timeline, and builds credibility by knowing the neighborhoods, tax implications, and lifestyle trade-offs they’re weighing. This is not volume work; it’s precision work, and it pays accordingly.

Does the brokerage you start with matter?

More than the town you pick. Your license must be held by a broker, and that brokerage decides your training, tools, and support in the make-or-break first year. A recognized local name carries real weight. Sellers trust it before you say a word.

Why start your real estate career with Adams, Cameron & Co.?

Adams, Cameron & Co. has been the area's largest brokerage since 1963, with around 300 agents and offices across Volusia and Flagler County serving New Smyrna Beach. New agents get in-house marketing at no cost, seven-day non-competing manager support, structured training, and the global Leading Real Estate Companies of the World referral network, the credibility that matters in a higher-end coastal market.

What is your next step?

Read the licensing guide, see the neighborhoods worth knowing in our New Smyrna Beach neighborhood guide, go deeper on the town’s real story in our full history of New Smyrna Beach, then start a conversation with Adams, Cameron & Co. No pressure, just a clear picture of the path.
